plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous ornamental tree that covers its bare branches in clouds of pale pink to nearly white five-petaled flowers before the leaves emerge. It is the iconic tree of hanami (flower viewing) festivals and is planted in parks and along rivers and streets across temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to early April in Japan; mid-March to April in temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Japan, Korea, Washington D.C. (USA), temperate regions of Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Japan's Meteorological Agency tracks a 'cherry blossom front' (sakura zensen) that moves north across the country, and the trees in Tokyo are declared in bloom when just five to six blossoms open on the reference tree at Yasukuni Shrine.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped golden-yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals, and narrow blue-green leaves. It grows in woodlands, meadows, and hedgerows and is the ancestor of many garden daffodil cultivars.
plants.location: Western Europe, including England, Wales, France, and Spain; widely naturalized and cultivated elsewhere
plants.funFact: Daffodil bulbs contain the alkaloid galantamine, which has been developed into a medication used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia × soulangeana
plants.description: A small deciduous tree or large shrub bearing large, goblet-shaped flowers that open on bare branches in early spring. The blooms are white to deep pink-purple and can reach 10-15 cm across.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early spring (March to April) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Cultivated across temperate regions of North America, Europe, and East Asia; hybrid originated in France
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, and their flowers evolved before bees existed, so they are pollinated primarily by beetles, which is why the petals are tough and leathery.

plants.name: Nerine sarniensis
plants.commonName: Guernsey Lily (relatives such as Nerine bowdenii bloom in autumn); and Amaryllis belladonna, the Belladonna Lily
plants.description: Amaryllis belladonna is a bulbous perennial that sends up leafless stalks topped with clusters of fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, the autumn equinox period brings its peak flowering, after the leaves have died back in summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (February to April) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Western Cape of South Africa; naturalized in Australia, New Zealand, and California
plants.funFact: Because the flower stalks appear suddenly without any leaves, belladonna lilies are often called 'naked ladies' or 'March lilies' in the Southern Hemisphere.
